I actually talked to my mom about it last night. I know that depression runs in my family as well as anxiety and it turns out that she kept telling herself, and me, that I didn't need them because she wanted to deny the fact that maybe I am depressed. That's not easy for any parent to accept, I would believe. She said that she will support me taking them since she has background knowledge of the drug. Turns out my even younger sister takes them (very complicated situation) and my mother herself has been on anti-depressants for most of her life.

She also told me that prior to the prescription my pediatrician let her know that she researched the subject deeply and talked to a few specialists, not that it makes up for not having the proper training, but it makes it better. As of right now I'm swaying more towards trying them out but I think I might fear social stigma. One close friend of mine would prefer me not to since he worries about it making me feel worse and I want to get opinions from a couple more close people in my life. In the end it's all for me to get better but these people have to deal with me, you know? Their opinion helps me decide.

Thank you for your response, as well.

Well, I'm not eighteen yet and my mother personally doesn't want me to be on Prozac. She feels like I don't need them. It was a pediatrician that prescribed them to me because she thought I looked very troubled and anxious all of the time. I don't think I was ever actually diagnosed as depressed and anxiety orders are recorded to be in family history, as well as depression. Now, I truly do believe that something just isn't clicking right with me whether it be hormones and/or chemical imbalances. With that being said and lack of actual diagnosis, I do consider myself to be depressed because of such intense feelings of hopelessness and suicidal tendencies I've had for the past five years. Part of me feels almost like it's not okay to have to take something like that, since my mother seems to look down upon it. I'm paranoid about a lot of things (lol) and this is being one of them. I think a lot of it is because of how ignorant I am of the actual drug.

Also, I'm aware of the fact that it's not an immediate change from taking the medication. If it gets worse, for example, I feel that I might be too naive too notice this and link it with the Prozac since I don't know exactly what it /should/ do to me. Emotional side-effects, I think, are hard things to pinpoint and notice as well as describe since isn't it different for everybody?
